key_insight: ScaFE turns LLM knowledge into local, executable scar-feature programs for more data-efficient and auditable classification than direct end-to-end or VLM-based diagnosis.
clinical_relevance: This approach could help hospitals classify keloids vs hypertrophic scars across sites while keeping patient images local and preserving traceability for governance and review.
method: LLM retrieves clinical evidence and generates deterministic feature programs for visually assessable scar attributes.
Programs run locally; only aggregated validation metrics and SHAP summaries are used to iteratively repair features.
A lightweight Random Forest classifies the resulting structured features.
evidence_signal: On 600 photos from three hospitals with leave-one-site-out evaluation, ScaFE reached 81.0% site-macro balanced accuracy and beat the strongest baseline (BiomedCLIP) by 10.0 points; with 10% of development data it still achieved 72.0%.
watch_item: Performance depends on the quality of generated features and local validation, so broader external validation is needed before routine deployment.
paper_title: ScaFE: Data-Efficient Scar Classification with LLM-Generated Clinical Feature Programs
